titleEn: How to File a Renovation Insurance Claim in British Columbia

contentEn:
When damage hits your BC home, knowing how your insurance works means the difference between a smooth payout and a months-long dispute with your insurer. In BC, home renovation insurance claims are governed by the Insurance Act and reviewed by the Financial Institutions Regulatory Authority (BCFIRA). Reno Stars has helped dozens of Greater Vancouver homeowners document damage, complete the claim forms correctly, and get their restorations underway without delay.

The BC Insurance Act sets a hard 12-month deadline from the date of loss to file your claim. If you miss that window, your insurer can legally deny payment regardless of how valid your claim is. Document everything immediately, because the insurer's adjuster will ask for receipts, photos, and contractor estimates before authorizing any payout.

What does a standard BC home renovation insurance policy actually cover?

BC home insurance policies typically cover damage caused by fire, smoke, water escaping from pipes or appliances, windstorms, and falling objects. They do not cover damage from gradual leaks that went unreported, rot that resulted from deferred maintenance, or renovations done without the proper permits. The difference matters: a burst poly-B pipe that soaked your kitchen floor overnight is a covered peril; the slow drip under your sink that caused mold over six months is typically excluded as maintenance failure.

Your policy also carries a deductible — the amount you pay before coverage kicks in. Most BC homeowners carry a $1,000 deductible, though higher deductibles lower your premium. If your claim is for $22,000 in water damage and your deductible is $1,000, the insurer sends $21,000 if the claim is approved.

Does insurance pay for a full kitchen or bathroom renovation in BC?

Insurance covers the cost to restore your home to its pre-loss condition, not to upgrade it. If your ten-year-old kitchen was destroyed by a covered peril, the insurer pays depreciated value for a ten-year-old kitchen, not the cost of a brand-new one. If you want upgrades beyond what insurance covers, you pay the difference yourself. How long does a BC home renovation insurance claim take?

Simple claims with complete documentation can close in four to six weeks. Complex claims involving structural damage, liability disputes, or multiple contractors commonly take three to six months. BCFIRA data shows roughly 18% of closed claims involve a dispute, which extends the timeline significantly.

If your insurer's offer is too low, you have the right under the Insurance Act to demand an appraisal, file a complaint with BCFIRA, or enter mediation. Keep every piece of written communication from day one. Reno Stars provides detailed line-by-line estimates that support your position in disputes.

What if your claim is underpaid or denied?

BC homeowners have the right under the Insurance Act to demand an appraisal, file a complaint with BCFIRA, or enter mediation. Each route has costs and timelines. Keep every piece of written communication from the day the loss occurs. Reno Stars can provide detailed estimates that support your position in a dispute.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the deadline to file a renovation insurance claim in BC?

Under the BC Insurance Act, you have 12 months from the date of loss to file your claim. Filing early is always better — delays can complicate evidence collection and give insurers grounds to question the validity of late-reported damage.

Does insurance cover unpermitted renovation work?

No. Unpermitted renovation work is a standard exclusion in BC home insurance policies. Always obtain the required permits before starting any renovation work in the Greater Vancouver area.

Will insurance pay for a full kitchen if only part of it is damaged?

Insurance pays only for the damaged portion. If a burst pipe ruined your lower cabinets but your upper cabinets were undamaged, the insurer pays for lower-cabinet replacement only. A detailed contractor estimate helps document exactly what was damaged.

Can homeowners hire their own contractor instead of the insurer's preferred vendor?

Yes. BC homeowners have the right to hire any licensed contractor, including Reno Stars, and to submit that estimate as part of the claim documentation.

BC住宅装修保险通常涵盖哪些范围？

BC省标准家庭保险政策通常涵盖火灾、烟雾、水管或电器漏水、风灾和坠落物造成的损坏。不涵盖的范围包括：未及时报告的渐进性渗漏、长期维护不当导致的腐烂，以及无许可证装修工程。《保险法》明确指出，被保险人有责任在合理时间内修复损坏部位。

大多数BC房主的基本免赔额为1,000加元。如果理赔金额为22,000加元，免赔额为1,000加元，则保险公司赔付21,000加元。

保险是否支付完整厨房或浴室装修费用？

保险仅覆盖恢复至损失前状态的费用，而非升级改造。若十年前的厨房因管道爆裂全损，保险公司按当时同类标准材料折旧值赔偿，房主若想升级需自费。Reno Stars可提供详细的分项估算，为理赔过程提供专业支持。

常见问题

BC省装修保险理赔的时效是多久？

根据BC省《保险法》，从损失发生之日起，您有12个月的时间提交保险理赔。越早提交越好，因为延迟会增加举证难度。

无许可证的装修工程保险是否覆盖？

不覆盖。无许可证装修工程是保险除外责任。在大温哥华地区进行任何装修工程前，务必申请所需许可证。

部分损坏时保险是否支付完整厨房装修？

保险仅覆盖实际损坏范围。若爆裂管道仅损坏了下柜，上柜完好，保险公司只赔付下柜更换费用。

业主是否可以聘请自己的承包商而非保险公司指定的供应商？

可以。BC省房主有权选择任何持牌承包商，包括Reno Stars，并提交其估算报告作为理赔文件的一部分。
